hints: Adjacent suffixes either start with different letters or compare by the ranks of their remaining tails.
For each suffix use the given rank of its next-position suffix, with the empty tail ranked first.
Increase the assigned letter whenever those tail ranks fail to increase.
analogy: Adjacent suffixes can share a first letter only if their remaining tails already appear in the required order.
example: Suffix order [3,1,2] is realized by aba: suffixes a, aba, ba are sorted.
algorithm: Build the inverse rank of the supplied suffix array, assigning the empty suffix rank -1. Traverse suffixes in the given order, starting with letter a. For consecutive starts u,v, increase the letter if rank[u+1] > rank[v+1], treating position n+1 as the empty suffix. Assign that letter to position v. If more than 26 letters are needed print -1; otherwise print the assigned string.
correctness: Within one letter group suffix order must match the strict order of tail ranks, so every descent forces a letter increase. Increasing exactly at those descents uses the fewest letters and makes every adjacent suffix pair ordered; hence the whole suffix array is correct.
complexity: For n suffixes, O(n) time and O(n) space.
